text:
incident-bot: ALERT: kv-cache mem surge + continuous-batcher tail-latency spike in us-west-2 (cluster infer-ww2). Alert cb-8471. 95p latency for /v1/generate jumped from ~120ms -> ~2.3s, error rate + client timeouts starting. Affected pools: shared-hosted, fallback routing triggered for some requests.

olivia (oncall): seeing the same in graphs. spike started ~1801234500. requests with mixed short+long sequences look to be causing big KV cache churn and huge batch assembly delays. starting live triage.

raj (eng-runtime): on it. preliminary hypothesis: continuous-batching fairness regression combined with a kv-cache retention change that increased entry size, causing paging and slow batch formation for short requests. can we isolate long-running requests?

dana (sre): can we temporarily route long/cheap requests to dedicated pool or throttle long sequence length? any quick mitigation we can flip?

olivia (oncall): pushing a short-term mitigation: reduce continuous_batcher max_batch_size and tighten max_wait_ms to prioritize latency for short requests. also will enable soft eviction on kv_cache to prevent cache blowups. deploying to us-west-2 canary now.

raj (eng-runtime): exact patch i'm about to apply:
```json
{"continuous_batcher": {"max_batch_size": 32, "max_wait_ms": 6}, "kv_cache": {"soft_eviction": true, "max_entries": 250000}}
```

raj (eng-runtime): deploy command: `redwoodctl patch cluster infer-ww2 --json - <<EOF` then paste above. canary to 10% of pods.

olivia (oncall): canary is up (10% pods). metrics look promising: p95 dropped from 2.3s -> 420ms on canary. continuing rollout to 50%.

marta (customer-success): FYI we have 3 OL customers filed, ticket# 98712, 98715, 98728. they reported slow responses and one workspace retrying requests. CS team updated with current mitigation. We'll push a public status note if rollout is >30 min.

dana (sre): monitoring heap/paging: vmstat shows increased swap activity earlier, but after canary rollout swap I/O decreased on those pods. good sign. watch for new GC pauses.

olivia (oncall): rolling to 100% now. keeping traffic-weighted rollout (avoid cold-start spike).

incident-bot: Deployment cb-8471-hotfix started: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%.

raj (eng-runtime): quick temporary routing rule added: route requests with seq_len >= 2048 to dedicated-long-pool to avoid intermixing short/long in the same batcher. command: `redwoodctl route add --match "seq_len>=2048" --pool dedicated-long-pool --weight 1`

olivia (oncall): after 100% rollout p95 on affected routes stabilized ~360ms; error rate back to baseline. marking incident as mitigated.

marta (customer-success): I sent status update to the three customers and flagged for follow-up. one customer asked for retrospective + root cause.

raj (eng-runtime): root-cause notes in quick form: recent kv-cache retention PR increased per-entry size when metadata flags were added; combined with a scheduling regression in the continuous-batcher fairness logic that allowed a single long request to hold a batch longer, causing short requests to wait and kv-cache to accumulate hot prefixes. result = cache blowup + batch starvation.

dana (sre): actions: 1) revert or soft-roll metadata enlargement in kv-cache (PR id: 2438) 2) add microbench for entry-size regression 3) add scheduler fairness tests (short-vs-long mix) to CI 4) alert tuning for early kv-cache growth detection 5) run a canary with `max_batch_size=32` as default for mixed-traffic pools until we have a long-term scheduler fix.

olivia (oncall): handing off to raj for post-incident follow-through. I'm going offline in 20m.

raj (eng-runtime): taking handoff. I'll own the postmortem and the kv-cache PR. assign to eng-runtime + eng-sre. I'll also schedule an on-call playbook update for similar symptoms.

marta (customer-success): noted. please include a short customer-facing summary for CS (what we fixed, ETA for permanent fix).

olivia (oncall): thanks team. tagging this as P1 incident mitigated. follow-ups: postmortem owners: raj, dana, and olivia for timeline verification. ETA for next status update: 2026-03-16 14:00 UTC. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident cb-8471 status changed to MITIGATED by olivia (oncall) at 1801234620.

raj (eng-runtime): final note: patch that reduced batch size will be reverted once scheduler fairness fix is merged; keeping soft_eviction until we verify memory profile. creating follow-up tasks now.
